The cluster is explicitly a CCAP-gene-expression-defined class (per Luan et al. 2006, the same driver/reference tradition FBbt uses to define this class), not a single morphological cell type. FBbt:00111316 'adult CCAP neuron' is defined at exactly this level -- any adult neuron expressing CCAP -- matching the report's own conclusion that class-level granularity is the honest target. Adult stage is correct for this atlas (whole adult brain, ages 1-30 days). The cluster is well corroborated within the paper (independent res-8.0 cluster 151, same literature marker), supporting high confidence despite the small cell number.

FBbt defines 'CCHamide-1 neuron' at exactly the gene-expression-class level that this cluster represents -- any neuron expressing CCHa1 -- with no stage restriction, so no development-stage mismatch. However, unlike CCAP/Hug/Gr43a, this cluster has weak internal evidentiary support (no Table S2 direct annotation beyond 'Unannotated', no res-8.0 cross-check, and several non-peptidergic co-markers alongside CCHa1), so although the biological identity denoted by label and term match, confidence in this specific cluster genuinely representing CCHa1 neurons is low.

This FBbt term's defining criteria (adult nervous system, peptide-hormone-secreting, expresses Capa) match the cluster's defining marker and neurosecretory character exactly, and critically it is not restricted to the VNC/abdominal-ganglion 'Va neuron' subtype - it covers any adult Capa-expressing neuron anywhere in the nervous system, including the brain. This resolves the report's own brain-vs-VNC caveat: the general adult Capability neuron term is the correct level for a brain-resident Capa+ population, since the more specific classic 'Va neuron' terms are VNC/abdominal-ganglion-restricted and would not apply to whole-brain-derived cells.
Authors name corazonin neurons; FBbt adult corazonin neuron is the same type.

FBbt has no generic 'FMRFamide neuron' gene-expression class (unlike its CCAP/CCHamide-1/corazonin/Ms/GPA2-GPB5 neuron classes) -- only two specific, disambiguated FMRFamide-expressing interneuron subtypes (FMRFamide SE2 neuron, FBbt:00001981; FMRFamide SE3 neuron, FBbt:00100392), each a single named subesophageal-zone cell type. This transcriptomic cluster explicitly cannot be resolved to either of those (or to any other single FMRFa+ type): the report's own analysis concludes FMRFa marks a co-expression class spanning ~90 distinct neurons of many types, and the honest target is a broad, non-specific parent. 'Adult peptidergic neuron' is the best defensible common parent covering this heterogeneous population; a more specific FBbt term would misrepresent the data even if one existed.

FBbt does not further split 'adult Hugin neuron' into hugin-PC/VNC/RG subtypes at the adult stage (that subtype resolution exists only for larval Hugin neuron in FBbt), so 'adult Hugin neuron' is the finest FBbt term available at the adult stage and matches the resolution of this transcriptomic cluster exactly -- both are the general SEZ hugin-expressing population, unresolved to projection-target subtype. The paper's main text explicitly and independently identifies this exact population ('Hug neurons from the subesophageal ganglion'), giving high confidence. Adult stage is correct for this whole-adult-brain atlas.

fbbt_label: adult insulin secreting cell of pars intercerebralis
justification: Both the cluster's defining markers (Ilp2, Ilp3, Ilp5 co-expression) and its identity (insulin-producing cells of the pars intercerebralis) match this FBbt term's defining criteria precisely. The paper's own annotation (Brogiolo et al. 2001; Rulifson et al. 2002) independently converges with the classic IPC literature underlying the FBbt term. Same biology under different labels (GEO cluster name 'IPC' vs. FBbt anatomical term) is an exact match per mapping guidance; the adult-stage-qualified FBbt term is appropriate since Davie et al. 2018 profiles adult brains only.

The report explicitly recommends treating this cluster at marker-defined granularity as 'ITP-expressing neurons', not as a resolved specific anatomical subtype - this matches FBbt:00048313 'ITP neuron' exactly, which is itself defined purely by ITP expression (plus neurosecretory character) with no further anatomical restriction. No adult-stage-qualified version of this general term exists in FBbt, but the general term is not stage-restricted so it applies cleanly to this adult cluster. Confidence is medium rather than high because the cluster's small size and ambiguous origin leave it unclear which of the several known ITP+ populations (clock-associated LNd/LN ITP neuron, or other neurosecretory ITP+ cells) it represents, though this uncertainty is intrinsic to the FBbt term's own generality, not a mismatch.

FBbt:00004046 'LNv neuron' is defined at exactly the resolution achieved by this cluster: the whole ventral-LN population (sLNv + lLNv, ~9 cells/hemisphere, predominantly Pdf-expressing) of the adult brain, without splitting into sLNv/lLNv subtypes. This matches the report's own conclusion that a term covering 'Pdf-expressing lateral ventral neurons' (parent of sLNv/lLNv) is the honest mapping level, since the paper's description does not distinguish the two morphological subtypes within this subcluster. Location (accessory medulla association) and function (locomotor rhythm pacemaking via Pdf) both align closely.

justification: The cluster's discriminating marker (sNPF+, trio+) and lobe assignment (mushroom body gamma lobe, adult brain, class-N intrinsic MB neuron) match FBbt:00049828 'adult gamma Kenyon cell' exactly: same neuropil target (gamma lobe), same adult developmental stage, and the FBbt definition itself cites sNPF expression as a defining marker, matching the paper's own discriminating logic. FBbt further subdivides adult gamma KCs into gamma-main/gamma-dorsal/gamma-s1-4 subtypes (from connectomic studies, e.g. Li et al. 2020), but the report explicitly states the atlas could not resolve any finer subtype within the lobe (subclustering separated cells by technical covariates, not biology), so the whole-lobe adult gamma Kenyon cell term is the correct and complete level of resolution for this cluster.

The FBbt definition (adult CNS glia with dendritic morphology that elaborates within the synaptic neuropil) matches the report's description of astrocyte-like glia as the main neuropil-infiltrating astrocytic glial cell type of the adult brain, supporting synaptic function and analogous to vertebrate astrocytes. Both are defined at the same level of specificity: FBbt:00047841 is the general adult (brain-wide) astrocyte-like glial cell class, and the report explicitly states the paper does not split this cluster into central-brain vs optic-lobe subpopulations, so the general adult term is the correct level rather than the more specific 'adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell' (FBbt:00047885) or 'adult optic lobe astrocyte-like glial cell' (FBbt:00049808) children.

The FBbt definition's glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity (Konstantinides et al., 2022) matches the report's own independent observation of VGlut expression in this cluster's top markers, giving convergent support beyond the label match alone. The label itself is unambiguous (GEO = Table S2, method: mapping to Konstantinides et al. 2018, no REVIEW flag), and the general TmY morphology (medulla+lobula processes) matches the report's description. Confidence is medium rather than high because the specific 'TmY14' identity in this dataset rests solely on cross-dataset transcriptomic mapping (no independent literature markers/driver lines cited by the authors for this cluster specifically), so while the label and neurotransmitter class both check out, subtype-level certainty depends on the external atlas correspondence.

The cluster is an explicitly merged group: transcriptomically indistinguishable Pm1 and Pm2 cells (svp/Lim3+, Vsx1-), not a single established cell type. FBbt has distinct, well-defined terms for the individual types - 'proximal medullary amacrine neuron Pm1' (FBbt:00003833) and 'proximal medullary amacrine neuron Pm2' (FBbt:00003835) - both GABAergic per scRNAseq lineage assignment (Konstantinides et al., 2022), matching the report's biology, but neither alone correctly represents this mixed cluster, and FBbt has no term denoting the Pm1+Pm2 grouping specifically. The most specific common parent of Pm1 and Pm2 in FBbt is 'proximal medullary amacrine neuron' (FBbt:00003832, the Pm class), which both are direct children of. This parent is an honest, correctly-leveled broad match: it captures the shared proximal-medulla amacrine identity and (via its GABAergic Pm1/Pm2/Pm3/Pm7/Pm8/Pm10/Pm11 children) the general biology, but is broader than the report's Vsx1-negative (i.e. non-Pm3) restriction since it also subsumes Pm3 and other Pm subtypes not present in this cluster.

The FBbt definition (adult CNS glia elaborating along the outer surface of neuropil and surrounding tracts/commissures) matches the report's description of ensheathing glia forming thin sheaths around neuropil compartments and axon tracts. Both are at the same, brain-wide granularity: the report explicitly notes the paper does not state whether central-brain and optic-lobe ensheathing glia are transcriptomically distinguished in this cluster, so the general adult term (rather than 'adult central brain ensheathing glial cell' FBbt:00047886 or 'adult optic lobe ensheathing glial cell' FBbt:00058224) is the honest match.
Authors name Mip neurons; adult-specific Mip neuron term is the exact class.

The authors' call is a group of lamina monopolar neuron types L1-L5, so the most specific common parent is lamina monopolar neuron (FBbt:00003718). OLS ancestors of L4 (FBbt:00003722) and L5 (FBbt:00003725) include it; L1-L3 are its children. The term is adult-specific by definition.

Unlike gamma and alpha'/beta' Kenyon cells, FBbt has no separate 'larval alpha/beta Kenyon cell' term because alpha/beta KCs are generated only during the pupal stage and exist solely in the adult mushroom body; FBbt:00100248 'alpha/beta Kenyon cell' is therefore already the adult-specific concept, directly parented under 'adult Kenyon cell' and 'sNPF neuron'. Its definition matches the report's discriminating marker (sNPF-positive) and neuropil (alpha/beta lobes) exactly. FBbt further distinguishes core/surface/posterior alpha/beta KC subtypes from connectomic studies, but the report explicitly states this atlas could not resolve any finer subtype (subclustering separated on technical covariates only), so the whole-lobe term is the correct and complete level.

T4 (FBbt:00003731) and T5 (FBbt:00003736) are both direct children of 'T neuron' (FBbt:00003726) in FBbt, matching the report's description of two distinct T-type columnar neurons (different input layers/pathways) that this cluster genuinely cannot separate. No FBbt term exists that specifically groups only T4+T5 (e.g. no 'T4/T5 direction-selective neuron' term was found), so the honest, most specific common parent is the general 'T neuron' class. This is a true merged-group case (both Table S2 and GEO agree on the merge; the authors state the four subtypes of each cannot be resolved), so a broad match at this level is the correct call, not a workaround for weak evidence -- both flags are false.

The FBbt term cites the same Hasegawa et al. (2011) source the Davie et al. paper itself uses to identify Mi1 by hth+bsh co-expression, and both describe the same medulla intrinsic columnar neuron with M1/M5/M9-M10 arborization. Label provenance is unambiguous (GEO = Table S2, literature markers/mapping, no REVIEW flag). This is an adult brain atlas; FBbt:00003776 is the mature/adult form and no immature-specific term is needed.

The authors' call is a group (adPN and lPN). The most specific common FBbt parent is adult antennal lobe projection neuron (FBbt:00067123): OLS hierarchical ancestors of both adPN (FBbt:00007438) and lPN (FBbt:00007439) include it. 'adult olfactory projection neuron' (FBbt:00051299) was NOT found among the ancestors of either, so it is not a valid parent.

The cluster's discriminating marker (trio+, sNPF-, plus DAT as a distinguishing marker per the paper's Fig S3G-H) and neuropil (alpha'/beta' lobes, adult brain) match FBbt:00049834 'adult alpha'/beta' Kenyon cell' exactly. This atlas is adult tissue and the FBbt term is explicitly the adult form (developing with little alteration from the larval alpha'/beta' KC during metamorphosis). FBbt further subdivides into anterior-posterior/middle subtypes from connectomic studies, but the report states no finer subtype resolution was achieved in this atlas (subclustering separated on technical covariates only), so the whole-lobe adult term is the correct and complete level.

FBbt:00006048 'pacemaker neuron' (parent of FBbt:00100163) defines the class by exactly the criterion used to identify this cluster: molecular oscillation of Period/Timeless expression that supports diurnal-rhythm control - matching the tim/Clk/cry/vri marker signature and 'circadian pacemaker neuron' function described in the report. FBbt:00100163 restricts this to the adult nervous system, matching the confirmed adult tissue. The remainder cluster is explicitly a class-level mixture of several named clock-neuron subgroups (LNd, DN2, DN3, LPN) with no further transcriptomic separation, so per dataset guidance for remainder labels the class-level pacemaker-neuron term is the correct (honest) mapping level, not any single subgroup. Confidence is medium rather than high because 'pacemaker neuron' is a functional/molecular class definition rather than a dedicated 'circadian clock neuron of adult brain' anatomy term, and because DN1 residual contamination cannot be ruled out.

The FBbt definition of columnar neuron T1 matches the report's anatomy point for point: medulla cell body, T-shaped fiber, arborization in M1-M2, climbing fibers into the lamina cartridge. This is the same classical Fischbach and Dittrich (1989) morphological type the paper cites for its own T1 identification (Hamanaka and Meinertzhagen 2010 builds on this). Label provenance is unambiguous (GEO = Table S2, no REVIEW flag), and the cluster is described as clean/single-identity. This is an adult brain atlas and FBbt:00003727 is the (implicitly adult) mature form; no separate 'adult T1 neuron' term exists, and no immature-specific term is warranted since the cluster spans 0-30 days post-eclosion (mature adult).

The cluster is explicitly a neurotransmitter-class-level grouping (many anatomically distinct serotonergic types merged, per the report's own mapping notes), not a single morphological cell type. FBbt:00049526 'adult serotonergic neuron' is defined at exactly this class level ('any serotonergic neuron of the adult') and covers the adult central brain distribution described (protocerebrum, SEZ, antennal lobe, mushroom body, optic lobe). Since the report itself states the honest mapping level is a broad serotonergic-neuron class term, the class-level FBbt term is the correct (not merely broad) match for this class-level cluster.

The authors' GEO label names the single type Tm5c; FBbt has a non-obsolete adult term for it (transmedullary neuron Tm5c, FBbt:00110074). Taken at face value under the 'composed primarily of' relation.

Tm5a (FBbt:00110072) and Tm5b (FBbt:00110073) are both direct children of 'transmedullary neuron Tm5' (FBbt:00003793) in FBbt, and both are cholinergic transmedullary neurons receiving R7 input and terminating in the lobula -- matching the report's description of Tm5a/Tm5b as cholinergic, R7/R8-associated, medulla-to-lobula relay neurons distinct from the glutamatergic Tm5c. This FBbt parent term is exactly the 'Tm5ab' grouping (i.e. Tm5 minus Tm5c), making it a precisely-fitting common parent rather than an overly broad fallback. No FBbt term specifically labelled 'Tm5ab' exists, so this is the correct, most specific broad match.
The authors name the general class 'Dopaminergic', and the data are adult; the adult-specific class term adult dopaminergic neuron is the exact match.

This is a non-CNS blood cell type incidentally captured in the dissected adult brain sample, per the report and per the dataset-specific guidance that hemocyte/plasmatocyte clusters should be mapped as real cell types rather than excluded. The report confirms the cells are adult (0-50 days post-eclosion) plasmatocytes marked by Hml and phagocytic/ECM genes, matching FBbt's 'adult plasmatocyte' definition exactly (adult-stage hemocyte, originates embryonically/larvally, does not divide in adult). The GEO label 'Plasmatocytes' is noted in the report as a curator-applied synonym for the authors' broader Table S2 'Hemocytes' annotation, consistent with plasmatocytes being the dominant expected hemocyte type in this context.

Tm1 (FBbt:00003789, a transmedullary neuron) and TmY8 (FBbt:00003826, a transmedullary Y neuron, itself a child of 'transmedullary neuron') share 'transmedullary neuron' as their most specific common ancestor in FBbt. This matches the report's framing exactly: two anatomically distinct types (a classical narrow-field Tm and a wide-field TmY) that this cluster cannot separate because no distinguishing markers were found, only cross-dataset mapping. No FBbt term groups specifically 'Tm1+TmY8'. This is a genuine merged group intrinsic to the data, not an artifact of curation or weak evidence, so a broad match at this level is the correct, honest call.

This is an explicit remainder/class-level label per the report: the authors themselves describe it as a mixed, unresolved pool of dimm-positive peptidergic neurons rather than a single anatomical cell type. FBbt:00058202 'adult peptidergic neuron' (any peptidergic neuron of the adult) is defined at exactly this class level - the correct and honest target for an unresolved remainder group - so the label mismatch (driver/marker-based grouping vs. ontology class term) does not downgrade this to a broad match; the cluster IS this class, just not resolved further.

This cluster is explicitly documented as a coarse, unresolved three-way merge of the Pm1, Pm2 and Pm3 proximal-medulla amacrine neuron types (Vsx1+ Pm3 cells not separable from svp+ Pm1/Pm2 cells at this resolution). FBbt has separate, more specific terms for each named subtype (Pm1 = FBbt:00003833, Pm2 = FBbt:00003835, Pm3 = FBbt:00110066), but none of these individually represents the merged group, and FBbt has no single term denoting the specific 'Pm1+Pm2+Pm3' grouping. The most specific FBbt term that genuinely covers all three cell types as a shared IS-A parent is 'proximal medullary amacrine neuron' (FBbt:00003832), the direct parent of Pm1, Pm2 and Pm3 (and also of other Pm subtypes, e.g. Pm4-Pm13, not represented in this cluster). Its definition (medulla-intrinsic amacrine neuron with soma in adjacent cortex, projecting through the proximal medulla surface to form wide terminal arbors mainly restricted to one layer) matches the report's location (medulla, proximal layers) and general morphology, though it does not itself specify GABAergic identity the way the individual Pm1-3 terms do post-Konstantinides 2022. This is an honest broad match: the FBbt term is a valid, correctly-specific-as-possible parent given the merged/unresolved nature of the cluster, not a downgrade due to label mismatch. Pm1, Pm2 and Pm3 individual terms are listed in other_candidates and rejected because attributing the merged 316-cell cluster to any single one of them would misrepresent the data.

No FBbt search for 'cortex glia' returned a differently-named term, confirming 'cell body glial cell' is the corresponding FBbt anatomy class. The 'adult brain' qualifier matches this being a whole-brain (central brain + optic lobe) unresolved pool, the same granularity as the report describes.

FBbt has no term for Poxn-expressing neurons, nor for either of the two specific anatomical populations named in the source text (the protocerebral dorsal Poxn+ cluster or the deutocerebral ventral Poxn+ cluster of Boll and Noll, 2002 / Minocha et al., 2017) - searches for 'Poxn', 'Pox neuro', 'protocerebral dorsal cluster', and 'deutocerebral ventral cluster' returned no relevant hits in FBbt. The report itself flags that this 99-cell transcriptomic cluster likely merges/subsets the ~350-cell combined population and recommends a common-parent mapping level rather than forcing a specific anatomical identity. Boll and Noll (2002) and Minocha et al. (2017) characterize these Poxn+ cells as adult brain interneurons, and the cluster's mixed dopaminergic (Dat) and GABAergic (Gad1/Rdl) marker signature is consistent with interneuron identity spanning more than one population. 'adult interneuron' (FBbt:00052046) captures the confirmed cell-type level (interneuron, adult CNS) without asserting a specific brain region or subtype that the transcriptomic cluster itself cannot resolve. This is a genuine broad match: the cluster is almost certainly more specific than 'adult interneuron' (it corresponds to Poxn+ cells of one or both named anatomical groups) but no such specific FBbt term exists for curators to select.

The FBbt definition (adult glia located in the optic chiasm, arranged between the outer and inner chiasmata) matches the report's description of chiasm glia as an optic-lobe-specific glial population associated with the optic chiasmata. FBbt does have more specific children ('adult inner optic chiasma giant glial cell' FBbt:00100527 and 'adult outer optic chiasma giant glial cell' FBbt:00100526), but the report explicitly states the paper does not distinguish outer vs. inner chiasm glia for this cluster - so the general 'adult optic chiasma glial cell' parent is the correct, honest resolution level rather than a broad match to an over-general term; it is the specific term this cluster's own granularity supports.

author_conflict: Table S2 calls this cluster 'Subperineurial Glia'
justification: The FBbt definition (outer perineurial sheath glial cell sitting on top of the subperineurial layer at the adult brain surface) matches the report's description of perineurial glia as the outermost surface-glia layer of the blood-brain barrier, external to subperineurial glia. The dominant majority of this GEO cluster (200/259 cells, from res-2.0 cluster 70) is cleanly annotated 'Perineurial glia' by the authors and matches this FBbt term exactly. Confidence is downgraded from high to medium (not downgraded to broad match, since the FBbt term itself is correct for the bulk of the cluster) because the report's REVIEW flag documents that a real minority (59/259 cells, ~23%) of this GEO cluster are, by the authors' own S2 annotation, subperineurial glia (res-2.0 cluster 85) rather than perineurial - i.e. the cluster as delivered is not a perfectly pure population.

FBbt:00003629 'DN1 neuron' is defined at exactly the resolution achieved here: the whole DN1 dorsal clock-neuron group of the adult brain, without splitting into DN1a/DN1p. This matches the report's own conclusion that 'DN1' as a parent grouping term is the honest mapping level, with markers (Dh31, CNMa) favouring DN1p-dominance but insufficient evidence to exclude DN1a. Label, location (dorsal, near pars intercerebralis) and clock-circuit role align directly.

FBbt does not carry a separate 'dorsal cluster neuron' class; searches for 'DCN' and 'dorsal cluster neuron(s)' return exactly the same 4 LC14-branch terms as searching 'LC14', confirming FBbt has fully merged the DCN literature into the lobula columnar LC14 nomenclature (embedding '(dorsal cluster)' as a parenthetical synonym inside the definitions of FBbt:00100486 and its child terms). FBbt:00100486 'lobula columnar neuron LC14' is defined directly from Hassan et al. 2000 (dorsal soma location between optic lobe and central brain; ato expression) plus Srahna et al. 2006 (contralateral projection via the great commissure to the lobula) - the same two founding papers the report cites for this cluster's identity, with matching defining criteria (ato marker, dorsal soma location, contralateral commissural projection, ~22-68/hemisphere vs. report's ~40/hemisphere, 98 observed). The report's own cross-reference to LC14 (Wu et al., 2016) is corroborated: FBbt treats LC14 and DCN as the same cell type, not distinct concepts. The scRNAseq cluster does not resolve axon-target subtypes (contralateral-lobula-only vs. contralateral-medulla vs. immature), so the whole-population parent term FBbt:00100486 (not a stage/subtype-specific child) is the correct level of granularity, matching the report's single undifferentiated cluster. This is adult data and FBbt:00100486 covers the mature/adult population (its subtype children are the stage/target-specific refinements). Given provenance from the same founding papers with matching criteria, this is classified as an exact match with both new_term_needed and verification_needed set to false.

This FBbt term's defining criteria (adult nervous system, peptide-hormone-secreting, expresses Capa) match the cluster's defining marker and neurosecretory character exactly, and critically it is not restricted to the VNC/abdominal-ganglion 'Va neuron' subtype - it covers any adult Capa-expressing neuron anywhere in the nervous system, including the brain. This resolves the report's own brain-vs-VNC caveat: the general adult Capability neuron term is the correct level for a brain-resident Capa+ population, since the more specific classic 'Va neuron' terms are VNC/abdominal-ganglion-restricted and would not apply to whole-brain-derived cells.

fbbt_label: sugar-sensing neuron of the adult brain
justification: This FBbt term was defined from the same source (Miyamoto and Amrein, 2014) and the same defining criteria (Gr43a fructose-sensing, co-expression with corazonin/Crz, adult brain location) that the Davie et al. 2018 paper itself cites for this cluster -- the paper explicitly cross-references the same Miyamoto and Amrein (2014) identification. Per the provenance rule for same-paper-derived subtypes, this counts as an exact match rather than a verification case: the ontology term and this cluster denote the same, independently corroborated cell type (paper's own res-8.0 cluster 129 'Gr43a neurons', matching literature reference). This is the strongest-supported cluster among the neuropeptide subclusters in this dataset.

The cluster is explicitly a CCAP-gene-expression-defined class (per Luan et al. 2006, the same driver/reference tradition FBbt uses to define this class), not a single morphological cell type. FBbt:00111316 'adult CCAP neuron' is defined at exactly this level -- any adult neuron expressing CCAP -- matching the report's own conclusion that class-level granularity is the honest target. Adult stage is correct for this atlas (whole adult brain, ages 1-30 days). The cluster is well corroborated within the paper (independent res-8.0 cluster 151, same literature marker), supporting high confidence despite the small cell number.

FBbt:00003719 is glutamatergic, postsynaptic to outer photoreceptors R1-6 in the lamina, and part of the classical L1/L2/L3/L4/L5 lamina monopolar set -- matching the report's VGlut-based, ON-pathway identity point for point. This is an adult brain atlas (0-50 days post-eclosion) and L1 is a well-established, singular Drosophila cell type with no merging in this cluster, so the mature adult term is the correct level (no separate 'adult L1' term exists; the FBbt term is implicitly the adult/mature form, distinct from 'immature lamina monopolar neuron L1' FBbt:00053... which would apply only to developing/pupal stages). The one caveat noted in the report -- that Table S3 marker evidence is for the undifferentiated parent cluster, not L1-specific -- concerns the strength of the underlying subclustering call, not the FBbt term match itself, which is unambiguous once the L1 identity is accepted.

FBbt:00003720 is postsynaptic to R1-R6 in the lamina and presynaptic to Tm1/Tm2 in medulla layer M2, exactly the OFF-pathway relay role described in the report. This is an adult brain atlas and L2 is a well-established, singular cell type, not merged with any other type in this cluster, so the mature adult term is the correct level (no separate adult-specific variant exists beyond this term; the immature form would only apply to a developing/pupal atlas). The report's caveat that the L2 call rests on regression-model similarity rather than a literature marker, with only parent-cluster (undifferentiated) marker evidence in Table S3, affects confidence in the subclustering call but not the anatomical identity of the FBbt term itself, which is anatomically uncontroversial as stated in the report's own mapping notes.

FBbt:00003721 terminates in medulla layer M3 and is postsynaptic to outer photoreceptors R1-R6, matching the report's description of L3 as the sustained, achromatic relay terminating in M3. This is an adult brain atlas and L3 is a well-established, singular cell type not merged with any other type in this cluster, so the mature adult term is the correct level. As with L2, the report flags that the L3 call rests on regression-model similarity rather than a literature marker gene and that Table S3 marker evidence is for the undifferentiated parent cluster; this bears on confidence in the subclustering call, not on the anatomical correctness of the FBbt term once L3 identity is accepted.

FBbt has individual terms for lamina monopolar neuron L4 (FBbt:00003722) and L5 (FBbt:00003725), but no single FBbt term denoting the joint 'L4 and L5' grouping the GEO/paper cluster actually represents. Per dataset guidance for merged-group labels, the honest mapping is the most specific common parent -- 'lamina monopolar neuron' (FBbt:00003718), which both L4 and L5 are direct children of -- rather than picking one specific subtype and overstating the resolution this cluster provides. The individual L4 and L5 terms are listed as candidates for reference but rejected as the single best_match because assigning either alone would claim a split the paper's own bsh-based subclustering did not perform.
Authors name lamina monopolar neurons; class term is exact.

This label is explicitly the unresolved remainder of cluster 27 - cells not assigned to any finer lineage or marker group. Its identity IS 'olfactory projection neuron' at the class level; nothing in the report supports resolving it further (no lineage, no marker combination). FBbt:00051299 'adult olfactory projection neuron' captures exactly this level: an adult neuron relaying olfactory information to higher brain centers, matching the report's location (antennal lobe -> mushroom body calyx / lateral horn) and function. Adult-specific term chosen per dataset guidance (whole adult brain, 0-50 days). This is the correct/honest mapping level for a remainder label, not an artificial downgrade.

fbbt_label: adult antennal lobe projection neuron adPN
justification: FBbt:00007438 is defined exactly at the lineage level this cluster occupies: all antennal lobe PNs derived from the anterodorsal neuroblast (ALad1), matching the report's description of adPN origin, uniglomerular dendrites, mALT/iACT axon tract, and lateral horn/calyx targets. The cluster carries no finer marker information (C15/kn), so no more specific FBbt term (e.g. individual glomerular adPN types, or the C15+/kn+ subgroup terms, which do not exist in FBbt) can be justified. Same biology as the FBbt lineage class, different naming convention (driver/lineage label vs formal FBbt term) - genuine exact match, not a forced generalisation.

fbbt_label: adult antennal lobe projection neuron adPN
justification: FBbt has no term built on the C15 marker or citing Li et al. 2017 / Davie et al. 2018 for this specific subgroup (searched directly - no hits). The report itself concludes this is a transcriptomic subgroup of the adPN lineage of uncertain correspondence to a specific glomerular PN type; only 6 of the many PN classes Li et al. (2017) profiled were 'unequivocally mapped' to a known glomerulus, and whether C15(+) adPNs is one of these is not established. The cluster IS-A adult antennal lobe projection neuron adPN (FBbt:00007438) but carries a distinguishing marker (C15) that FBbt does not capture at any level, so this is an honest broad match rather than an exact one.

fbbt_label: adult antennal lobe projection neuron adPN
justification: No FBbt term is built on the C15/kn combinatorial marker code or cites Li et al. 2017 / Davie et al. 2018 for this subgroup (searched directly - no hits). The report concludes this is a transcriptomic subgroup of uncertain anatomical granularity, noting its comparatively large size (131 cells) may indicate it spans more than one closely related PN type rather than a single glomerular class. The cluster IS-A adult antennal lobe projection neuron adPN (FBbt:00007438) but the distinguishing C15+/kn+ combination is not captured by any FBbt term, making this an honest broad match.

fbbt_label: adult antennal lobe projection neuron adPN
justification: No FBbt term is built on the kn (knot/collier) marker or cites Li et al. 2017 / Davie et al. 2018 for this subgroup (searched directly - no hits). The report concludes it is not established whether kn(+) adPNs is one of the six PN classes Li et al. (2017) 'unequivocally mapped' to a known glomerulus, so it should be treated as a transcriptomic subgroup of uncertain specificity rather than a confirmed single named cell type. The cluster IS-A adult antennal lobe projection neuron adPN (FBbt:00007438) but the distinguishing kn+ marker is not captured by any FBbt term.

This label is not a genuine, reproducible cell type as described by the authors: it is absent from Table S2, its marker combination (kn+/CG31676+) mixes an adPN marker with an lPN marker in a way not discussed in the paper text, and its label_validation.tsv provenance note appears mismatched (referencing an unrelated neuropeptide-reclustering method). The report explicitly recommends treating it as unresolved/uncertain - possibly doublets, transitional cells, or a curation artefact - and, if a mapping is required at all, using the most honest general level: 'olfactory projection neuron'. Given the lineage ambiguity (adPN vs lPN marker overlap), even the lineage-level adPN/lPN terms cannot be safely assigned, so the broader OPN class term is the only defensible anchor. Both adPN and lPN lineage terms are listed as rejected candidates below since either specific lineage assignment would overstate what the data support.

fbbt_label: adult antennal lobe projection neuron lPN
justification: FBbt:00007439 is defined exactly at the lineage level this cluster occupies: all antennal lobe PNs derived from the lateral neuroblast (ALl1) dorsal hemilineage, matching the report's lPN lineage, lateral cell body position, and mACT axon tract to lateral horn/calyx. Unlike FBbt:00047312 (restricted to uniglomerular lPNs), FBbt:00007439 is not glomerular-pattern restricted, matching the report's note that lPNs include both uni- and multiglomerular types. The cluster carries no unpg/CG31676 marker information, so no finer FBbt term is available or justified.

Per dataset guidance, this is a 'remainder' label (cells of the dopaminergic class not resolved to a subtype after PAM was pulled out) and the correct honest mapping level is the class term itself, not any of the individually-named DAN clusters (PPL1, PPL2ab, PPM1/2, PPM3, PAL) it mixes. FBbt:00058206 'adult dopaminergic neuron' is exactly this class-level term restricted to adult tissue, matching the report's central-brain, adult, dopamine-releasing description. Note this term is broader than the true underlying biology (~7 named DAN clusters) but that breadth is honest given the atlas provides no further resolution.

This FBbt term describes exactly the whole-PAM-cluster level of resolution achieved in the atlas: a single dopaminergic neuron population with cell bodies in the anterior (inferior) medial protocerebrum, comprising multiple subtypes not distinguished here, all following a mushroom body commissure. This matches the report's own conclusion that the correct mapping level is the PAM-cluster parent, not any of the ~15 individual compartment-specific PAM subtypes (e.g. PAM01-PAM15, individually defined by different criteria such as MB commissure position in Li et al. 2020/Otto et al. 2020 - not the source of this cluster).

This is a class-level, neurotransmitter-defined cluster (Tbh+ subset of Tdc2+ neurons) explicitly not resolved to any anatomical subtype by the atlas. FBbt:00058203 'adult octopaminergic neuron' is the class-level FBbt term at exactly this resolution, restricted to adult tissue matching the confirmed adult (0-50 day) atlas. Per dataset guidance, remainder/class-level clusters map to the class term as the correct (not merely broad) level.
